name: Sobekhotep III
summary:
Sobekhotep III was the ruler of Egypt during the mid-Thirteenth Dynasty, succeeding his father, Sekhemre Sewadjtawy Sobekhotep II. He reigned for four years and implemented various economic reforms to stabilize the kingdom.

As king, Sobekhotep III oversaw significant architectural projects, including the construction of temples and tombs at Thebes. His reign also saw a resurgence in trade with neighboring countries, particularly Nubia and Syria.

Despite his efforts to revitalize Egypt's economy, Sobekhotep III's dynasty ultimately declined due to internal conflicts and external pressures from neighboring powers. He died around 1800 BCE, marking the end of an era for this Egyptian kingdom.

Sobekhotep III's legacy can be seen in the architectural achievements of his reign, which continue to inspire wonder and admiration today.
